_comment: Diet engine quality baseline. Re-recorded after the whole-app fresh dive. Two deliberate trades are priced into these numbers. (1) A substitution may no longer replace the ingredient a dish is named after, and the rule now matches plurals and multi-word names, so 'Lentil Soup (Chickpeas instead of Lentils)' cannot be served; it also reads the English column, so it is no longer silently off for Arabic requests. (2) Candidate ORDER is computed on a structure score bounded below the value of an explicit choice, because role, cuisine and library membership summed to more than a choice is worth and a food the client never named could lead the list ahead of one they did. `scores` keeps the real numbers, so the judge that weighs a dish against a plate is unchanged. Together these cost dish rate (0.845 -> 0.79) and a little chosen share, and buy: no dish served without its namesake ingredient, and the client's choices always at the head of their own lists. min_distinct_portions_per_food is measured over engine-BUILT plates only, because a recipe author's pinned clove of garlic is meant to be identical every time and counting it made the metric unmeasurable.
